evidence.why: Complete entry body shows guard, assignment, state arguments and callback publication.

facts.rationale: Replaces an unsupported upward-launch guarantee with exact guarded assignment and callback ordering.
facts.value: Clears cmd_vars[0]. If u.kb.x64 is false, assigns specials_aerial_vertical_momentum to self_vel.y and sets x64 true; otherwise it leaves vertical velocity unchanged locally. It then requests ftKb_MS_SpecialAirS with arguments 0, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, NULL, calls ftAnim_8006EBA4, and installs fn_800F53AC as accessory4_cb. The velocity assignment is not additive and has no sign or finite-value check. Repeated entry while x64 stays true does not reapply it; a universal once-per-airtime invariant is not established here.

evidence.why: Shows nonzero guard, nullable cleanup, flag reset and landing arguments.

facts.rationale: Preserves exact local behavior and includes the independently verified optional callee branch and float boundary.
facts.value: Calls ft_80081D0C and performs its move-local cleanup only for a nonzero result: destroys and clears a non-NULL u.kb.hat.x0, unconditionally clears u.kb.x64, and requests ftCo_LandingFallSpecial_Enter(gobj, false, specials_landing_lag). The landing callee can instead choose HammerLanding; otherwise it uses (0.1F + fp->x2EC) / landing_lag as animation rate. Neither this caller nor that calculation validates zero, negative, infinite or NaN lag. Exact map-query contact polarity is not inferred from the GroundOrAir enum names.

Consumers establish star geometry, descriptor and velocity roles.

facts.rationale: Records complete owned-TU scope without assigning unproved section contents or adopting rendered aliases.
facts.value: Implements Kirby's ground/air SpecialS Hammer entry and action callbacks, a shared command-driven Hammer article lifecycle with diagnostic callback-conflict checking, and SpecialN helpers that export fighter position, scaled victim-star collision bounds, post-star velocity parameters and an HSD_Joint accessory descriptor. Source-level diagnostic arrays are present, but compiled section contents and object-layout equivalences remain unresolved.
